verdict.rationale: PayPal's Store Sync defines a machine-readable catalog feed (Google Product Feed / OpenAI ACP Product Feed) with required fields for id, title, link (checkout link), image_link, description, price, and availability, and each row represents a product variant — directly matching the story's data elements. However this is a merchant-published feed gated behind a form-based access-approval process, not an open read API a developer can query for 'any listed product' across the platform, and Store Sync itself is scoped only to US physical goods in USD. Missing for 10: a public/queryable read endpoint for arbitrary listed products without merchant onboarding, and confirmation that variant-level data is queryable beyond the feed file itself.
